script:
Shi Hengming
Shi Hengming didn't join Fengbo Temple from the beginning. He grew up in a social organization, and only when he left this organization did he learn it was a cult. He never knew the name of the cult leader who raised him. The leader taught him to read, write, and conduct himself, but used near-brainwashing methods. When Hengming gradually learned about the world through other means, he began to hate this man who had been manipulating his life, leaving him powerless to resist.
When police raided the cult, the leader heard the news early and escaped. Hengming disguised himself as a deceived victim and escaped, finally gaining freedom. After mixing in the outside world for more than ten years, he found he could never integrate into society and was even imprisoned for stealing money. After being released from prison, not knowing how to live, he came to Fengbo Temple in the suburbs, wanting to renounce the world. But when he entered Fengbo Temple, he discovered that the abbot was actually the man who had ruined his life, now with the Buddhist name Yankong.
Hengming knew that Yankong was very vigilant, and ordinary methods couldn't harm him at all. He had to catch him off guard. So he joined Fengbo Temple, preparing to find an opportunity to get his deep revenge. After all these years, Yankong still didn't recognize Hengming.
He had great talent for Buddhist teachings, and Yankong took very good care of him, often personally guiding him. Soon Hengming gained high prestige among his peers.
Yankong continued his previous cult practices, making money openly in the temple. He built a residential area in the temple called Quchenju, where various male and female lay disciples lived. Hengming often followed Yankong around and noticed that Yankong had very close contact with a female disciple named Zhang Qingzhu.
A person of the same generation as Yankong with equally high prestige in the temple had the Buddhist name Yanren. After contact with Yanren, Hengming found that Yanren was a truly devout monk who was very opposed to Yankong's profit-seeking behavior using Buddhism.
A year ago, someone moved into Quchenju - reportedly a well-known local investor named Zhao Zhengwei. Others didn't know, but Hengming was clear that this person must have been called by Yankong to develop this "Buddhist business" together. Hengming found Zhao Zhengwei very familiar but couldn't remember where he'd seen him.
Early this year, Hengming heard from believers that this person's family member had been bitten by a rabid dog and didn't get vaccinated in time, dying of rabies recently. This gave Hengming an idea.
Yankong loved keeping pets and had taken in several stray cats and dogs at the temple, making everyone think he was compassionate. Hengming found a pet dog outside and brought it back. He knew that the first thing Yankong did every morning after waking up was to recite the Heart Sutra once while lying in bed. So he trained this dog to bite people's hands when it heard the last part of the Heart Sutra.
This was difficult work because you couldn't train such a complex command from the start - it had to be learned step by step. It wasn't until July this year that the dog had learned it thoroughly. Then Hengming, using the excuse of going down the mountain, bought a bottle of deadly snake venom online.
On the evening of August 2nd, Hengming brought the dog to Yankong's residence. He had previously smeared snake venom on the dog. As long as Yankong petted the dog and then got bitten by it, the snake venom would naturally enter his body through the wound and kill him. Since snake venom is essentially protein, even if the dog ate the poison, as long as there were no wounds in its esophagus and stomach, it could digest and break down the venom without fatal effects.
He knocked on Yankong's door, left the dog there, and hid nearby. Yankong opened the door, saw the dog, and indeed let it into his room.
[August 3rd Morning]
At 4 AM this morning, Hengming went to Yankong's residence. On the way, he met Zhao Zhengwei, and they exchanged "Amitabha" greetings before parting. Arriving at Yankong's place, Hengming peeked inside. At this time, Yankong had already gotten up and started chanting. When he reached the last line, the dog rushed up and bit Yankong's hand hard. Yankong was shocked, shook off the dog, cursed a few times, then began cleaning the wound and washing up. Hengming waited for a long time but didn't see Yankong show signs of poisoning, and became very anxious. But then someone suddenly called him from behind, startling Hengming. He turned to see it was Master Uncle Yanren. Hengming claimed he came to call the abbot for morning prayers and hurriedly left.
At 5 o'clock, after all the monks gathered in the prayer hall, Yankong came to the abbot's seat, picked up the wooden fish mallet and prayer beads, and began leading everyone in chanting. But after just a short while, Yankong's voice suddenly stopped, his whole body convulsed, his face turned purple, he foamed at the mouth, and collapsed to the ground. When everyone rushed over, Yankong had already stopped breathing. Hengming was very puzzled - this deadly snake venom couldn't possibly take so long to take effect!
acts_goal: Do not proactively reveal that Zhao Zhengwei seemed very familiar to Hengming.
